last_mile_analysis.summary: Architecture is proven and solid. Remaining issues are projection edge cases, not architectural problems.

bare_function_names.cause: QualifyFuncRefs doesn't catch recursive functions (LetRec) or functions defined in nested let-chains inside lambdas
bare_function_names.fix: Extend flattenValue to handle LetRec at all levels; collect function names from Core program declarations

stdlib_functions.cause: std_list__Map, std_string__Trim, etc. — AILANG stdlib functions have no Go implementation
stdlib_functions.fix: Generate runtime bridge with Go implementations of stdlib functions, or use embedded evaluator for stdlib

cross_module_calls.cause: Module prefix mismatch between how definitions are named vs how cross-module GlobalRef is emitted
cross_module_calls.fix: Normalize module naming between lowerer and emitter

tmp_variable_ordering.cause: flattenValue doesn't recurse into all Core expression types (Match, If inside Let values)
tmp_variable_ordering.fix: Deeper recursion in flattenValue for all expression types that produce statements

external_packages.cause: References to external AILANG packages (pkg_sunholo_*) that don't exist in generated code
external_packages.fix: Either generate stubs or use FFI bridge to actual Go packages

adt_constructors.cause: _adt__Make_Block_* naming pattern from old codegen doesn't match new NewXxxYyy pattern
adt_constructors.fix: Normalize ADT constructor emission to match types.go definitions

builtin_dict_ops.cause: DictApp resolution incomplete for some type class methods (Fractional, Ord comparisons)
builtin_dict_ops.fix: Extend lowerDictMethod with more type class + method combinations

builtin_functions.cause: _builtin__Concat_String etc. — core builtins need Go implementations
builtin_functions.fix: Generate runtime bridge or inline during lowering

tuple_types.cause: Tuple2 struct not defined in generated types.go
tuple_types.fix: Emit TupleN structs in types.go for used arities

design_committee_questions: Should we continue chasing go build (Option B: more lowering fixes + runtime bridge)?
Or pivot to Option F (hybrid: evaluator for stdlib, emitter for pure functions)?
Or pivot to Option C (embedded evaluator library for deployment)?
The 90 stdlib stubs alone represent the 'superlinear maintenance burden' the design doc warned about.
The architecture (Statement IR) is proven and target-agnostic — the question is which target.
